verdict.rationale: The only on-topic evidence is the founder's comment that Hatchet multi-step workflows have an execution path declared ahead of time, plus general claims that it orchestrates durable workflows and coordinates worker execution. That suggests built-in multi-step composition, but the same comment notes you can't concatenate a bunch of futures to wait on later, and nothing documents parallel steps, dynamic fan-out/fan-in, or child workflows. missing for 10: documented parallel step execution, dynamic fan-out/fan-in over batches, child/sub-workflow spawning, first-party workflow-composition docs, hands-on corroboration

support.subject: As a backend developer, I compose workflows from parallel steps, fan-out/fan-in over dynamic batches, and child workflows without hand-rolling coordination

citations.quote: the execution path of a multi-step workflow in Hatchet is declared ahead of time
the central orchestration system that manages workflows, schedules tasks, and coordinates worker execution
